draft.title: Climate change and the economy
card: Greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide from burning coal, oil and gas, trap heat in the atmosphere. As emissions rise, average global temperatures tend to rise too.
Higher temperatures can bring more extreme weather, such as heatwaves, droughts, bushfires and floods. Sea levels also rise as the oceans warm and ice melts.
These changes impose costs on the economy. Farming can lose output when droughts or heat cut crop and livestock yields.
Health costs can rise with heat stress and smoke from bushfires. Infrastructure such as roads, homes and power lines can be damaged by floods, fires and storms, and repairs are costly.
draft.remember: Rising emissions can warm the climate, and the weather damage that follows costs farming, health and infrastructure.

a.q: Which chain of events best describes how rising emissions can harm an economy?
opts: More emissions, higher temperatures, extreme weather, costs
More emissions, cooler weather, fewer crops, higher costs
Higher temperatures, fewer emissions, weather damage, costs
Extreme weather, more emissions, then higher temperatures
a.why: Emissions trap heat, which raises temperatures. That can bring extreme weather, which damages farming, health and infrastructure. The second option wrongly says the climate cools when emissions rise.
a.clue: Start with the gases that trap heat, and end with the costs.

b.q: A long drought cuts wheat harvests on Sam's farm near Dubbo, and a bushfire later damages the power lines to his town. Which pair of costs does this show?
opts: Farming costs and infrastructure costs
Health costs and farming costs
Infrastructure costs and health costs
Farming costs and a fall in emissions
b.why: The lost wheat harvest is a farming cost. The damaged power lines are an infrastructure cost. Health costs can also follow from bushfires, but the case describes no health harm.
b.clue: Match the wheat and the power lines to the three areas on the card.

a.best: More emissions, higher temperatures, extreme weather, costs

problems.detail: The why refers to 'the second option' as the one that says the climate cools. The options are shown in a random order, and here the cooling option is third, so the why points students to the wrong option. It should name the option by its content, for example 'the option with cooler weather'.
